page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-capacity server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated virtual CPUs, which correspond to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-192 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read speeds reaching 12,787.43 GB/sec and uncached large-block write speeds of 247.9 GB/sec. The instance also excels in specialized workloads, achieving top-tier results in software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories, respectively.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers high compute density with dedicated CPU allocation, making it highly efficient for parallelized workloads. However, it lacks local NVMe storage and integrated GPU hardware, meaning storage-heavy or GPU-dependent tasks must rely on network-attached resources. Despite the lack of local storage, it delivers top-tier static web serving throughput of 227.94 GB/sec and handles 212.26 million Redis SET operations per second.

This server configuration is highly suitable for compute-intensive parallel processing, large-scale software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and memory-bound multi-threaded applications. The inclusion of Intel AMX also makes it capable of handling CPU-based LLM inference, as demonstrated by top-tier prompt processing speeds for large models.
